text:
security-oncall: Alerting — automated detector flagged a service-account token used from an unusual ASN. Possible access to model-artifacts bucket at 02:13 UTC. Pulling initial evidence now. :rotating_light:

alex: saw it, can you paste the raw event?

security-oncall: sure — event snippet:
```
event_time: 2026-03-20T02:13:22Z
service_account: svc-model-build-prod
action: objects.get
resource: s3://redwood-models/prod/gpt-latest/checkpoint.tar.gz
src_ip: 203.0.113.45
ua: curl/7.86.0
```

maya: 203.0.113.45 is an ASN we haven't seen in our fleet. Looks like a cloud provider in APAC. Could be botnet or feigned legit.

chris: i just revoked svc-model-build-prod tokens and rotated the CI role binding. blocked that IP at the edge and added a WAF rule. Confirmed no other tokens used in last 24h.

security-oncall: thanks. containment steps: 1) revoke tokens (done), 2) block IP (done), 3) disable service account until full audit, 4) run forensics on the artifact bucket, 5) prepare exec note.

alex: running bucket object audit now, listing all GETs from the last 72h, streaming to /tmp/s3-get-events.json

audit-bot: export job started — s3-get-events.json (partial) at 02:31 UTC. 14 GETs from svc-model-build-prod between 2026-03-19T23:00Z and 2026-03-20T02:14Z.

maya: we need to know if any artifacts were exfiltrated. If the attacker only read a small checkpoint file that's PII-free but still IP/provenance sensitive. Also flag for legal if customer data could be present.

ana: +1, tagging legal (ana).

ana: (Ana - Legal) on it. Need timeline and affected customers list before advising externally. Also confirm whether any keys or creds were stored in the artifact.

ana: quick Q: do we have E2E encryption on stored model artifacts?

alex: artifacts are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys. No customer data expected inside model checkpoints. But we do keep build notes/metadata in the same prefix occasionally. Investigating if any metadata files were touched.

chris: we mounted audit-collector for a full filesystem sweep of the build runner used by svc-model-build-prod. capturing process list and recent creds in memory snapshots.

security-oncall: status update: no writes observed, 4 unique object GETs of checkpoint and 2 metadata.json downloads. We'll need to parse metadata.json to see if secrets leaked.

maya: i'm running quick grep on metadata.json for patterns like "apikey" "secret" "TOKEN" — will report in 15m.

alex: draft of internal advisory for eng/product to limit churn: 
"Internal advisory: A service account token showed anomalous use from an unfamiliar IP. We have revoked the token, blocked the IP, and disabled the service account. Initial audit shows read-only access to two checkpoint files and two small metadata files. No evidence of customer data in the artifacts so far. Full forensic analysis in progress. Do not rotate unrelated credentials unless asked by Security. Do not share internal findings externally. We will provide a follow-up in 6 hours or earlier if new evidence emerges."

chris: looks good; add contact for escalation: security-oncall@redwood.internal and pager for oncall.

ana: legal suggested adding: "We are proactively investigating and have engaged forensic vendor X to assist. We will notify affected customers if we confirm any exposure of customer data."

jordan: CEO — thanks for the quick action. Please prepare an exec brief (1-slide) for the leadership sync at 09:00 PST. I want: timeline, scope, customer impact (yes/no), next steps.

security-oncall: on it. Draft exec bullet points: 
- 02:13 UTC: anomalous GET from svc-model-build-prod observed
- Immediate containment: token revoked, service account disabled, offending IP blocked
- Current scope: 4 artifact GETs, 2 metadata downloads; no writes detected
- Unknowns: whether metadata contained any credentials (analysis ongoing)
- Next steps: full forensic sweep, customers triage, external comms plan if needed

maya: drafting customer notification template (if needed). Short version for ops teams: 
"We are contacting you to report that a Redwood service account accessed certain model artifact files in your region on 2026-03-20. Our investigation so far shows read-only access and no evidence of customer data exposure. We have revoked the implicated credentials and are conducting a forensic review. We will notify you immediately if we confirm any exposure. Contact security@redwood.com for questions."

ana: please add legal contact info and a dedicated incident inbox to that template.

alex: for post-incident: recommend RBAC hardening — remove broad read scopes from build service accounts, enforce short-lived ephemeral creds for CI, add deny-listing for external ASNs, and enable object-level access logs to BigQuery for faster queries.

chris: also propose we add automated quarantining of any service account that does GETs from IPs not seen in the last 30 days.

security-oncall: agreed. putting action items into a post-incident ticket. For now, continuing forensic analysis — will update thread with final determination and a customer notification decision by 08:30 UTC. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
